subject: Connectivity fabric decision: PrivateLink vs Peering vs Site-to-site VPN (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Michael Yates <michael.yates@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem LLM access - high level connectivity question

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the earlier demo — our infra team is starting to map out the private deployment pattern for the on-prem inference stack. Before we commit to a POC topology, we want a concise recommendation from Redwood on the tradeoffs between: VPC peering, PrivateLink (interface endpoints), and a site-to-site VPN for accessing Redwood Private.

High-level constraints:
- Regulated patient PII in the requests (must stay within our network boundary where possible).
- Latency sensitivity for live triage flows (~100ms p50 target).
- We have an existing MPLS/SD-WAN between DCs and a transit VPC in AWS.
- Procurement prefers a single operational model but we can accept a hybrid approach for initial rollout.

Can you provide a short recommendation and a list of risks/operational tasks we should plan for? Also, any required network ACLs or firewall rules we must pre-open for the POC?

Thanks — Michael
Michael Yates
Director, Infrastructure
Acme Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Michael Yates <michael.yates@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: RE: On-prem LLM access - high level connectivity question

Michael — thanks for the context and the constraints. I pulled in Ben (account lead) and Kim (solutions engineer) to make sure we account for both commercial and technical tradeoffs.

Quick recommendation (TL;DR):
- For regulated, production traffic where you must limit exposure of PII, PrivateLink (interface endpoints) is our recommended starting point. It keeps traffic within AWS’ private networking and reduces blast radius.
- If you need the absolute lowest cloud-to-cloud latency and have full VPC control in both ends, VPC peering can be slightly faster and simpler for egress, but it’s less flexible (CIDR planning / transitive limitations) and not available across accounts with transitive routing without transit gateway.
- Site-to-site VPN is useful as a resilient fallback and for on-premises-only workloads, but expect higher and variable latency and more operational overhead (tunnels, rekeying, monitoring).

Risks / operational items to plan:
- PrivateLink: ensure acme’s subnet has available ENI capacity for interface endpoints; security groups must allow ENI egress to Redwood port(s). You’ll need to manage DNS for endpoint resolution.
- Peering: confirm CIDR overlap (no overlap allowed), and plan for route table updates. If your architecture uses a transit gateway, that changes the recommendation in favor of peering/transit attachments.
- VPN: establish tunnel capacity planning and BGP / routing policies; monitor jitter and packet loss for triage flows.

Attached is a short checklist and a crude network sketch to kick off the POC. Ben: any commercial notes to add (SLA, throughput tiers)? Kim: can you follow with a short ops-level checklist and port list?

Next steps I propose:
1) Short technical call (30 min) with Acme infra + Kim to confirm ENI/CIDR/DNS constraints.
2) Configure a PrivateLink POC endpoint (if Acme agrees) and run latency/quality tests.
3) If latency is unacceptable, evaluate peering/transit attachment as an alternate.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: On-prem LLM access - high level connectivity question

Michael — quick commercial context to help your procurement team:
- PrivateLink: typically rolled into Redwood Private onboarding. Slightly higher per-GB egress costs (cloud provider side) but operationally simpler and better for compliance controls.
- Peering/Transit: can reduce per-token cost in sustained high-throughput scenarios because traffic transit pricing is lower; however, we recommend contractual guardrails around throughput commitments (burst vs sustained).
- VPN: cheapest up-front but higher ops cost and unpredictable latency; we treat VPN as a non-prod/dev fallback in SLAs.

We can scope the POC as a 6-week engagement (config + 2-week load/latency test) with a simple uplift if you later want peering. I’ll share a draft SOW after Kim and Marissa confirm the technical checklist.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: On-prem LLM access - high level connectivity question

Hi team — I reviewed the network sketch you shared (thanks) and ran a quick checklist against Acme’s constraints. Below are concrete, actionable items for the POC plus a suggested measurement plan.

POC recommendation: start with PrivateLink + optional transit attachment test. PrivateLink keeps an explicit, auditable interface in your VPC and meets the compliance ask. If we hit p50 latency > 120ms, escalate to a peering/transit attachment test.

Firewall / network rules (minimum set):
- Allow outbound to Redwood Private IPs on TCP 443 (we use TLS for all control/data channels).
- Allow NTP (UDP 123) from the hosts that will perform latency tests.
- Open ephemeral egress for ENIs created by interface endpoints (security groups attached to endpoints).

Operational checklist:
- Confirm Acme VPC CIDR and available /27 for endpoint ENIs.
- Reserve DNS override for rdw-private.acme.internal -> interface endpoint private DNS.
- Create CloudWatch/Datadog test monitors for p50/p95 latency, jitter, and packet loss against the endpoint.
- Create a fallback runbook for failover to site-to-site VPN (include steps to re-route test traffic).

Measurement plan (initial 48 hours):
- Baseline: measure RTT over PrivateLink from 3 runner hosts at 1-min cadence for 24h.
- Load test: synthetic token-generation test at 10 QPS, 50 QPS for short bursts to observe queuing and p95 impact.
- If p50 > 120ms or p95 > 350ms, schedule peering test.

Attachments: I uploaded a short checklist and a sample latency CSV template you can use.

If this plan sounds good, can we lock a 30-min call early next week (Mon/Tue) to confirm CIDR and DNS?

Thanks,
Kim Park
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
